diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $c$ be a cost function such that for all particle $i$, $c_i : y\in \Omega \mapsto c(y,\bm{x}_i)\in [0,+\infty) $ belongs to $C^{1,1}(\Omega)$.

Optimal transport solvers are computer programs that take as input the weights $v_1$, \dots, $v_N$, the cost functions $c_1, \dots, c_N$, and return as output the unique vector of optimal values for the Kantorovitch potentials $(w_1, \dots, w_N)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Theorem 2 asserts two false/unsupported claims: First, that the weights w_i in R are uniquely defined such that |L_i| = v_i. In reality, shifting all w_i by an arbitrary constant C leaves c(x, x_i) - w_i <= c(x, x_j) - w_j completely unchanged, so (w_1 + C, ..., w_N + C) generates identical Laguerre cells and volumes for any C in R; potentials are only unique up to an additive constant. Second, assuming only c_i in C^{1,1}(Omega) is insufficient to guarantee that cell intersections have measure zero, that a unique Monge map exists, or that potentials satisfying the volume constraints exist (e.g., if c is constant or if c(y, x_i) - c(y, x_j) is constant on a set of positive measure). A standard twist/regularity condition (e.g., that level sets of differences have zero Lebesgue measure) is required.

failure_location.quote:
The intersection of two Laguerre cells has zero Lebesgue measure and the weights $w_i\in \mathbb{R}$, called Kantorovich potentials, are uniquely defined such that for all $i\in\{1,\ldots,N\},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:laguerrevolume}|\mathscr{L}_i| = v_i.\end{equation}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify that the Kantorovich potentials (w_1, ..., w_N) are unique up to an additive constant (or unique in R^N / R(1,...,1)), and include the standard twist/regularity condition on the cost function c.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness statement for Kantorovich potentials in Theorem 2 is false as stated, and the theorem statement lacks the standard twist condition required for existence and uniqueness of the semi-discrete Monge solution and the negligible overlap of Laguerre cells.
issues.title: Omitted twist condition and false uniqueness of Kantorovich potentials in semi-discrete OT theorem
issues.why_classification: Stating uniqueness up to an additive constant and adding the standard twist condition on c is a routine local fix that preserves the theorem and all downstream applications.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: First of all, since the function $U : w \mapsto |\mathscr{S}(w)|$ is non-decreasing, $U(0)=0$ and $U(w)\to1$ as $w\to+\infty$ there exists a unique $w^*>0$ such that $U(w^*) = v_i$. Then let $\mathscr{S}\subset\Omega$ be any shape of volume $v_i$.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 4 states that the shape S minimizing I(S) is a sublevel set S(w) for some w > 0, but omits the prerequisite volume constraint |S| = v_i. Without prescribing a fixed positive volume |S| = v_i, the unconstrained minimum of I(S) for non-negative cost c is the empty set S = emptyset (with energy 0). The proof explicitly assumes and uses the condition |S| = v_i, which was missing from the lemma's hypotheses.

failure_location.quote:
The shape $\mathscr{S}\subset\Omega$ that minimizes the individual energy 
\[\mathcal{I}(\mathscr{S}) = \int_{\mathscr{S}} c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i)\dd \bm{x}\]
is of the form 
\[\mathscr{S}(w) = \{\bm{x}\in\Omega,\,\, c(\bm{x},\bm{x}_i) \leq w\},\]
for some $w>0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the constraint |S| = v_i to the statement of Lemma 4 (minimizing I(S) over all shapes S subset Omega with |S| = v_i).
issues.overall_effect: As stated, Lemma 4 is false without fixing the volume of S. Restricting the minimization to shapes S satisfying |S| = v_i makes the statement consistent with its proof.
issues.title: Omission of volume constraint in preferred shape lemma statement
issues.why_classification: The omitted volume constraint is an immediate local fix already present in the proof; adding it requires no new proof architecture and completely restores the lemma.
